title: Micro-CT Imaging of Rat Stomach Vasculature
author: Deborah Jaffey
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bafnibme
materials: Administer the appropriate dose of ketamine/xylazine intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Animal Preparation and Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Prepare the rat and administer anesthesia based on body weight.

substeps.instruction: Feed the rat according to the 'Micro-CT imaging of iodine-stained rat stomach' protocol.
Weigh the rat to determine the dose of ketamine + xylazine cocktail (2-3 mL/kg body weight).
Prepare a cocktail of 10 mL of 100 mg/mL ketamine (Patterson Veterinary #07-803-6637) and 1 mL of 100 mg/mL xylazine (Akorn Inc #NDC: 59399-110-20) for a total volume of 11 mL.
Prepare two syringes: one with a 23G needle for intraperitoneal injection of the cocktail and one with a 26G needle for intracardiac injection of 500 USP units of heparin.

steps.title: Prepare Microfil Contrast Agent
steps.instruction: Mix the radiopaque compound and diluent in a non-glass, sealable container (at least 40 mL).

substeps.instruction: Use Microfil MV-122 (Flow Tech Inc #MV-122).
Mix using a ratio of 3 mL compound to 5 mL diluent.
Ensure the total volume exceeds the estimated blood volume of the rat while maintaining the 3:5 ratio.
Gently shake or stir to mix without producing bubbles.
Do not add the curing agent yet.

steps.title: Setup Perfusion Equipment
steps.instruction: Configure the peristalsis pump and surgical access.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a Masterflex series peristalsis pump with tubing accommodating an 18G blunted needle attached to a 1 mL syringe.
Set the pump flow rate to 25 mL/min.
Expose the thoracic cavity of the rat, keeping the abdomen closed to maintain a temperature near 37 °C.
Insert an infant feeding tube into the stomach through the esophagus (approx. 125 mm from mouth to LES for a 300 g male Sprague-Dawley rat) to keep the lower esophageal sphincter open.

steps.title: Vascular Perfusion
steps.instruction: Perform saline flush and Microfil injection while maintaining abdominal warmth.

substeps.instruction: Heat 1 liter of saline (sterile or 1L ultrapure water + 8.7 g NaCl) to 37 °C–42 °C.
Turn on the pump to flow saline through the 18G blunted needle.
Inject heparin into the left ventricle, then thread the 18G needle into the aorta.
Cut the right atrium and partially sever the inferior vena cava (IVC).
Administer warm saline in and around the abdominal cavity at least once per minute to prevent cooling.
Perfuse approximately 200 mL of saline.

steps.title: Microfil Polymerization and Injection
steps.instruction: Activate the curing agent and perfuse the contrast medium.

substeps.instruction: After 200 mL saline perfusion, add the curing agent to the Microfil solution (e.g., for 12 mL MV-122 and 20 mL diluent) and mix gently for 1 to 2 minutes.
Start a 20-minute timer immediately upon adding the curing agent.
After a total of 250 mL saline perfusion, stop the pump and move the input tubing into the Microfil solution.
Reduce pump rate to 2 mL/min and start the pump.
Continue pumping until the 20-minute timer expires or the solution is depleted, while continuing to apply warm saline to the abdomen.
Stop the pump, clamp the perfusion line and the IVC (distal to the cut), and wait at least 70 minutes for the compound to cure.

steps.title: Stomach Dissection and Fixation
steps.instruction: Extract the stomach and fix the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Open the abdomen and dissect the stomach, leaving ~1 cm of esophagus and duodenum.
Preserve the gastroepiploic artery along the greater curvature for orientation.
Immediately place the stomach in 4% paraformaldehyde (PF) in 0.01M PBS for at least 24 hours.

steps.title: Prepare Gelatin Support
steps.instruction: Create a suspension medium to prevent tissue distortion during scanning.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 4% to 5% type B gelatin solution in ultrapure water (40 g/L to 50 g/L).
Prepare the solution one day before scanning to allow cooling; refrigerate if blurred scans occur.
Use a 4-ounce, circular, transparent, polypropylene (PP) container with a sealable top.

steps.title: Stomach Preparation for Scanning
steps.instruction: Clean, orient, and inflate the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Remove the stomach from 4% PF and rinse with 10X PBS or saline.
Fill the PP container 3/4 full with gelatin.
Place the stomach ventral side up, esophagus facing the back, and pylorus facing left, lying as flat as possible; submerge completely.
Optional: Flush the stomach by massaging it under saline to remove food contents through the pylorus.
Fill the stomach with saline using a 5 Fr feeding tube attached to a 10 or 20 mL syringe filled with PBS, threading through the duodenum and pylorus.
Hold the duodenum skyward and plunge the syringe until bubbles stop emerging.
Slowly remove the tube while plunging until the distal end is at the junction of the index finger and thumb at the open end of the duodenum.
Clamp the duodenum with hemostats, tie a bow 2-3 mm proximal to the clamp, and remove the clamp.
Tie off the esophagus with a cotton thread bow, leaving at least 1 cm between the LES and the bow.

steps.title: Micro-CT Scanning
steps.instruction: Image the vasculature using the Quantum GX2 system.

substeps.instruction: Warm up the scanner (suggested: 55 kV, 144 µA).
Place the container on the bore between the beam and detector.
Use Live Mode to adjust translational position and minimize the field of view (FOV) to the smallest size that captures the whole stomach (typically 45 mm, sometimes 60 mm or 72 mm).
Set parameters to High Resolution with at least a 14-minute scan time and start the scan.
Transfer the stomach to a PP container with saline/PBS and rinse off all gelatin.
Remove tie-off threads and return stomachs to 4% PF stored at 4 °C.
Optional: For whole-stomach imaging, soak in I2/KI solution per the 'Micro-CT imaging of iodine-stained rat stomach' protocol starting from step 18.
